threads.thread_goal: Align on current routines, constraints, and select pilot group for the program.

messages.text: Hi team, welcome to the channel for our new Integrated Wellbeing Program. The goal is to pilot a more structured and supportive program for our youths. First step is to understand their current schedules. @36599, you're leading on T1, mapping their routines. Can you give us an update on where we can track this in A1?
Morning! I've already started on A1. I've documented the last few days and will have a full week mapped out by EOD. I'll drop the link here once it's ready for comments.
Thanks for kicking this off. How many youths are we thinking for the initial pilot group? Is there a target size?

Good question. I'd suggest we start with a small group of 4-5 to keep it manageable and allow for close observation. We should select youths who are likely to engage but also represent a range of needs.

Okay, here is the draft of A1 with the current routines. I've highlighted a few youths who have fewer external appointments and have shown interest in new activities before: specifically Anna, Leo, Sam, and Maria. What do you all think?
Thanks for sharing this so quickly! The list looks like a solid starting point. They are a good mix.

This is a great overview, thanks. I agree with the suggestions. One flag on Sam – his trauma-support sessions are on Wednesdays, so we need to ensure our program doesn't create emotional overload. We must keep that in mind when scheduling sensitive topics.
What about adding David? He's always asking about workshop activities.
Good thought, but David has mandatory tutoring every afternoon from 3-5pm, which is likely our main window for activities. Maybe he can join the next cohort?
Ah, right. I forgot about the tutoring. Next cohort sounds good.
So, are we agreed on the group being Anna, Leo, Sam, and Maria for the initial pilot? That's 4 youths.
Yes, that group seems appropriate, keeping the note about Sam in mind. Let's confirm that. D1.
Looking at A1, the most consistent free time for all four is weekdays between 3:00 PM and 5:00 PM, after school and before dinner prep.
That works. It avoids clashing with their school commitments.
Perfect. Let's lock in the 3-5 PM weekday window for our structured activities. D2. I can now start drafting a schedule based on this.
Great. I'll finalize T1 by adding a note in A1 confirming the pilot group and the agreed time slots.

threads.thread_goal: Design and finalize the weekly structured activity schedule and co-designed activities.

messages.text: Hi all, following our discussion, I've created a first draft of the weekly schedule, A5. It's based on the time windows we identified in A1. Please take a look and share your thoughts. This is the first version for T3.

Looks great! Just one small thing: the 'reflection circle' on Thursday at 4:45 PM might clash with dinner prep starting at 5. Maybe we can move it to 4:30? Also, I've started T6 and spoke with the group. They're really excited about a 'MasterChef' style cooking competition and a weekly movie night.
Thanks for sharing. Where in the schedule would the vocational skills sessions go?
I see @4543 has put 'Vocational Taster' placeholders on Tuesday and Thursday afternoons. We can firm those up once we decide on the modules in the other thread.
The cooking competition and movie night are fantastic ideas from the youths. How do we decide which ones to include?

Both are great suggestions. The cooking competition aligns well with developing practical life skills, and the movie night is a good option for relaxed social time. I suggest we add both. We can put the cooking competition in one of the vocational slots and the movie night on Friday evening. Does that sound good?
Perfect! They will be thrilled. That's D4 sorted then.

Good catch on the timing, I'll adjust the reflection circle. I've updated A5 to reflect that change and to include the two co-designed activities. Please take one last look. If there are no other major concerns, we can approve this initial schedule.
The updated A5 looks solid. It feels balanced between structure and leisure. I approve.
Looks good to me too.
Excellent. With that, we have an approved weekly schedule for the pilot. D3 is confirmed. I'll mark T3 as ready for implementation.

threads.thread_goal: Agree on templates and tools: individual plans, handover checklist, and monitoring log.

messages.text: Hi team, I've drafted the key documents for our pilot: A2 (Individual Support Plan), A4 (Shift Handover Checklist), and A7 (Wellbeing Monitoring Log). Links are in the message. Could you all take a look and provide feedback? This covers T2, T7, and T8.

Thanks for putting these together so fast! A4 looks really practical for handovers. Could we add a checkbox for 'Medication Administered / Refused'? That's a critical piece of info that sometimes gets missed in verbal updates.
The individual plan A2 seems very detailed. Are we sure staff will have enough time during a shift to fill all of this out for each youth?

That's a valid concern about workload. However, the sections in A2 are aligned with safeguarding requirements and best practices for holistic care. The intention isn't to complete it in one sitting, but to build it up over time. It's a living document. We'll need to be clear about that in the staff briefing (T10).

Looking at the monitoring log A7, the 1-5 scale for mood might be a bit subjective. Would a simpler 3-point scale like 'Positive', 'Neutral', 'Struggling' be quicker and more consistent for staff to use?

Excellent points, everyone. I've updated the documents. @36599, the medication checkbox is now in A4. @87939, I've changed the scale in A7 to the 3-point system. @4543, thanks for clarifying the use of A2. I've added a note at the top of the template to that effect.
The revisions are great. The tools are now more practical while retaining their purpose. I'm happy to approve A2 for use.
The checklist A4 is perfect now. And the simplified A7 log will be much easier to use consistently. I approve both.

Great. So we can confirm that the Individual Support Plan template is approved (D5), and we've agreed on the final versions of the handover checklist and monitoring indicators (D6). I'll mark T2, T7, and T8 as complete.

threads.thread_goal: Plan and coordinate vocational skills taster modules within the weekly schedule.

messages.text: Hi everyone, I've put together some ideas for the vocational skills tasters in A6, as part of T5. I'm suggesting 'Intro to Woodworking', 'Digital Art Basics', and 'Bike Repair'. Let me know what you think and when we could schedule them.

Bike repair is a brilliant idea, the youths will love getting their hands dirty! I'm a bit worried about woodworking though, it might require a higher staff-to-youth ratio for safety. Also, do we have the right software for digital art on the shared computers?

I share those concerns. Safety and resource constraints are key. For a pilot, we should prioritize low-risk, high-impact activities. The T5 description mentioned 'basic cooking' or 'CV basics' as examples. Could we perhaps substitute woodworking with one of those? Basic cooking, for instance, is a vital life skill and ties in nicely with the youths' 'MasterChef' idea.

Oh, I see. I didn't consider the supervision aspect for woodworking. That's a good point. Okay, I can definitely do a basic cooking module instead. So we'll go with 'Bike Repair' and 'Basic Cooking' for now?
Starting with those two sounds like a great plan. We can always introduce more complex modules later once the program is established. Let's confirm those two for the first pilot cycle.
Agreed. Let's lock in 'Basic Cooking' and 'Bike Repair' as our first two vocational modules. D7.
Great. Looking at the schedule A5, we have the vocational slots on Tuesdays and Thursdays from 3-5 PM. @87396, do those times work for you to run these sessions?
Yes, Tuesday and Thursday afternoons are perfect for me.
Excellent. So we'll schedule Basic Cooking for one of those slots and Bike Repair for the other. This is confirmed. D8. I will update A5 to reflect this. @87396, you can now prepare for T9.

threads.thread_goal: Review first two weeks of pilot, discuss incidents, and agree on adjustments.

messages.text: Team, we're two weeks into the pilot. I've compiled the feedback from staff and youths into a summary note (A8) as part of T11. I've also cross-referenced it with the trends from our monitoring log, A7. Please review and let's discuss adjustments.

Key takeaways from A8: The cooking module is a huge hit. However, engagement from Sam has been very low, and he's been disruptive in group settings. Also, Maria has missed all sessions due to a new external therapy schedule.

Yes, regarding Sam, we had an incident yesterday where he became very withdrawn. I followed the de-escalation steps in A3. My feeling is that the group environment is too stimulating for him at the moment. He's mentioned feeling watched.

That makes sense. What if we adapt our approach for him? We could offer him 1-on-1 sessions focused on his interests for the next couple of weeks, instead of the group activities. We can use his individual plan, A2, to structure and track this.

That's a good, person-centered adjustment. For Maria, it's unfortunate but her therapy must take priority. It probably makes sense to remove her from this pilot cohort to avoid setting her up for failure. We can always invite her to the next one.

I agree on both points. Let's adjust the pilot group composition: Sam will transition to a temporary 1-on-1 plan, and Maria will be withdrawn for now. This means we have a spot open. Leo has expressed a lot of interest; let's invite him to join. This is an adjustment to D1.
The feedback in A8 on the bike repair session was a bit mixed. It said attendance was low. Should we change it?

Yes, the few who came enjoyed it, but others said they wanted something more creative. In our last informal chat, they suggested a 'create a group playlist' session or a collaborative story writing workshop. The music idea got a lot of energy.

Let's be responsive to that feedback. It's a key part of the pilot. Pausing bike repair and replacing it with a 'group playlist' session seems like a smart move. It's low-resource and promotes positive self-expression. We can make that change for the next two weeks.
I can take the lead on planning the music session. I'll draft a simple outline and update the schedule. So we're agreed on modifying the co-designed activities based on this feedback (D4).
Perfect. Thanks for taking that on. I will handle the formal updates to the program documents as part of T12. Great discussion, team.
